definitions.gloss: background knowledge; prior knowledge; preliminary knowledge
definitions.explanation: Knowledge that one has or needs before engaging with a particular topic, task, or situation. Often mentioned when discussing what is needed to understand something.

examples.japanese: {予備知識|よびちしき}がなくても{楽|たの}しめる。
examples.english: You can enjoy it even without background knowledge.

examples.japanese: {予備知識|よびちしき}として{基本的|きほんてき}な{用語|ようご}を{説明|せつめい}します。
examples.english: I'll explain the basic terms as background knowledge.

examples.japanese: この{映画|えいが}は{歴史|れきし}の{予備知識|よびちしき}があるとより{深|ふか}く{理解|りかい}できる。
examples.english: You can understand this movie more deeply if you have some background knowledge of history.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound of {予備|よび} (preliminary, spare) and {知識|ちしき} (knowledge). Commonly used in educational and media contexts to describe what readers or viewers should know beforehand.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {予備知識|よびちしき}がある (to have background knowledge)
- {予備知識|よびちしき}がない (to lack background knowledge)
- {予備知識|よびちしき}なしで (without background knowledge)
- {予備知識|よびちしき}として (as background knowledge)
